sections.heading: How to Play Assassination
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Assassination"][color=c4]Assassination Rogue Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
The rotation for Assassination Rogue focuses on a simple build/spend rotation, but instead of optimizing around short cooldowns or swapping between buttons, Assassination is a slow spec, with purposeful downtime that rewards playing around the gaps in your rotation correctly.

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_creature_poison_02 size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c4]Preparing for AOE:[/color][/b] Our AoE is enabled through [spell=421975], [spell=381799], and [spell=1247227]. Crimson Tempest, especially, is a very expensive button in terms of energy, and knowing when AoE is going to happen in an encounter will allow you to plan around it with your cooldowns, bleeds, and resources.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_rogue_disembowel size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c4]Managing Envenom Uptime:[/color][/b] [spell=32645] grants a buff that is attached to numerous talents, such as [spell=455072]. Keeping uptime and managing this without overcapping resources will be the key to success.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_rogue_vigor size=medium type=round color=c4 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c4]Energy Efficiency:[/color][/b] Assassination is not locked by the GCD, and is instead locked by Energy. Because of this, you will want to think about what button is most efficient at a given time, rather than forcing yourself to cast something every time its possible.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=33081 icon=ability_rogue_deadlybrew]Assassination Rogue Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=ability_rogue_deadlybrew type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon][color=c4] Best Assassination Rogue Rotation[/color][/h2]
Assassination Rogue revolves around having multiple debuffs/buffs to maintain, followed by a simple build-and-spend rotation.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Assassination Rogue: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.
[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
	[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]

	[center]
	[wrapper width=95%]
		[grid column-width=49%]
			[display-option="deathstalker" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_deathstalkerrogue_deathstalkersmark]Deathstalker[/display-option]
			[display-option="fatebound" radio="Hero" icon=inv_ability_fateboundrogue_handoffateheads checked]Fatebound[/display-option]
		[/grid]
	[/wrapper]
	[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single-Target Priority" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]
	[h3 toc="Single Target Priority" type=bar][color=c4] Best Assassination Rogue Single Target Rotation[/color][/h3]
	[pad]
	Assassination in Single Target runs on a priority list, but it can be broken down more conceptually than other specs, which have hard rules for each button. Learning the overall situation of the fight and applying yourself to it will be better than trying to force very specific casts.[pad]
	[span display-options="deathstalker"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span][span display-options="fatebound"] With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-fatebound] [color=r1]Fatebound[/color] selected, the priority is as follows:[/span]


	[div display-options="!(deathstalker)&!(fatebound)"]
	[center][box border=true]
	[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate a Single Target priority[/b]
	[/box][/center]
	[/div]

[wrapper width=80%]
	[div display-options="deathstalker"]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3200]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]

	[h3 type=bar toc=false]Priority[/h3]
	[ol]
		[li]Maintain [spell=703][/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=5938] on cooldown[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=1329] until having 5 or more combo points[/li]

		[li]Cast [spell=32645] at [b]maximum[/b] combo points when [spell=457058] is active [span class=tip tooltip=darkest-fok][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
		[li]Maintain [spell=1943] by casting at 5 or more combo points[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=1856] followed by [spell=703] to apply [spell=381632]. This should be lined up with [spell=360194] in most situations [span class=tip tooltip=vanish-gar][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=360194] on cooldown[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=385627] on cooldown, immediately after [spell=360194] when applicable[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=32645] at 5 or more combo points[span class=tip tooltip=pooling][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
	[/ol]

		[section-header="Darkest Night" icon=spell_shadow_twilight collapse=true heading=none margin=1]
		[div][box level=2 display=block]
[large][color=c4]Impact of ~3% in total[/color][/large][pad]
		[spell=457058] asks that players finish with the maximum combo points to get the most out of the empowered Envenom. Darkest Night has a couple of additional caveats to watch for.
[ol][li]Do not cast [spell=1943] during Darkest Night outside of your opener. Doing so means Rupture isn't consuming a stack of [spell=457052] in the process. Letting Rupture drop entirely to facilitate this is acceptable.[/li]
[li][spell=455072] is a core part of our rotation around clipping Envenoms. It is okay to let Envenom drop while generating up to maximum combo points.[/li][/ol]
		[/box][/div]
		[/section-header]

		[section-header="Shiv Conditions" icon=inv_throwingknife_04 collapse=true heading=none margin=1]
		[div][box level=2 display=block]
[large][color=c4]Impact of ~2%[/color][/large][pad]
		[symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color] lacks significant resource generation compared to [symbol=wow-hero-talent-fatebound] [color=r1]Fatebound[/color], and as such, values energy efficiency much higher. Players should be looking to talent into [spell=1267182] in order to lower the cost of [spell=5938], making it by far the most efficient combo point generator available. Cast Shiv on cooldown in single target, but never with any adds up, as [spell=51723] becomes more efficient at that point.
		[/box][/div]
		[/section-header]

		[section-header="Fan of Knives" icon=ability_rogue_fanofknives collapse=true heading=none margin=1]
		[div][box level=2 display=block]
[large][color=c4]Impact of ~0.6%[/color][/large][pad]
		[symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color] significantly increases the strength of Fan of Knives through [spell=457067] and [spell=1248793]. If you are at 6 combo points with [spell=457058] currently active, pressing Fan of Knives is a small gain.
		[/box][/div]
		[/section-header]
	[/div]

	[div display-options="fatebound"]
	[wrapper][center][box border=true][center][small][i]The builds used below are covered in the [url guide=3200]Talents page[/url]. Anywhere you see the [span class=tip tooltip=NotesHighlight][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span] icon, you can hover over it for additional notes.[/i][/small][/center]
	[/box][/center]
	[/wrapper]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4]Priority[/color][/h3]
	[ol]
		[li]Maintain [spell=703][/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=1329] until having 5 or more combo points[/li]
		[li]Maintain [spell=1943] by casting at 5 or more combo points[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=1856] followed by [spell=703] to apply [spell=381632]. This should be lined up with [spell=360194] in most situations [span class=tip tooltip=vanish-gar][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=360194] on cooldown[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=385627] on cooldown, immediately after [spell=360194] when applicable[/li]
		[li]Cast [spell=32645] at 5 or more combo points[span class=tip tooltip=pooling][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-wrapper-turnin][/span][/li]
	[/ol]

		[section-header="Shiv Conditions" icon=inv_throwingknife_04 collapse=true heading=none margin=1]
		[div][box level=2 display=block]
[large][color=c4]Questionable/Difficult to guage[/color][/large][pad]
		[symbol=wow-hero-talent-fatebound] [color=r1]Fatebound[/color], unlike its purple counterpart, [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [color=night-fae]Deathstalker[/color], doesn't like pressing [spell=5938] nearly as much. Not only is it less resource-hungry, but [symbol=wow-hero-talent-fatebound] [color=r1]Fatebound[/color] also has [spell=454419], which significantly increases the value of non-Shiv generators. That being said, it [i]CAN[/i] still be an improvement to cast shiv on cooldown for Fatebound builds, especially if you are undergeared or pressing feint a lot.

This is left as a footnote because it is incredibly difficult to pin down who actually benefits from it. Testing through simulations and logs has shown Shiv to be both a significant (~1%) [color=red][i]LOSS[/i][/color] in DPS, but with perfect conditions and using Feint on cooldown, this loss can flip and turn out to be as high as a 4.5% gain. Because of the vast number of situations, gear/skill levels, and use cases for Feint/Crimson Vial, suggesting this as a hard rule for the spec is nearly impossible and could even be harmful for many players. You may see high-end players using Shiv on cooldown after assessing the content they are doing, but please do not treat this as a requirement or endorsement for everyone.
		[/box][/div]
		[/section-header]

	[/div]
[/wrapper]
[/tab]

[h3 toc="Opener" type=bar][color=rogue] Best Assassination Rogue Opener[/color][/h3]
[pad]
The Assassination Rogue opener is fairly standardized in Midnight and do not follow strict sequences as much as they follow conceptual ideas to prepare your cooldowns before executing on them. [span display-options="!(FB-Op)&!(DS-Op)"]You can use the buttons below to display openers for both single-target and AoE, depending on your chosen [b]Hero Talent[/b].[/span][span display-options="fatebound"]With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-fatebound] [b][color=druid]Fatebound[/color][/b] selected, opener details are as follows:[/span][span display-options="deathstalker"]With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-deathstalker] [b][color=warlock]Deathstalker[/color][/b] selected, opener details are as follows:[/span]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=rogue][icon name=ability_rogue_deathmark type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] Assassination Rogue Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Assassination has access to a variety of different cooldowns on its spec tree. They all come with extra wrinkles in how they work rather than being flat increases, so the section below covers [i]how[/i] they work and, most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Deathmark" icon=ability_rogue_deathmark]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue] Deathmark [/color][/h3]
[spell=360194] is a single-target debuff with a 2-minute cooldown. Aim to be casting it on cooldown and align all other cooldowns to it, as its interactions will dictate your burst. Deathmark has a number of effects:
[ul]
	[li]Applies a Bleed[/li]
	[li]Restores Energy[/li]
	[li]Increases the damage of [spell=703], [spell=1943], and Lethal Poisons such as [spell=2823] and [spell=381664][/li]
	[li]When a Lethal Poison is applied to the target, it is instead applied twice[/li]
[/ul]
The last two points are the most important to our burst. Increasing the damage of Garrote includes the empowered [spell=381632] from stealth, for example. Applying a Lethal Poison twice interacts with the ramping nature of [spell=385627], causing it to do significantly more damage.

Some other talents interact with Deathmark in passive ways, such as [spell=1249809] and [spell=381640]. This makes it both worth casting Deathmark for AoE and further empowers it as a single-target cooldown. 
[/tab]

[tab name="Kingsbane" icon=inv_knife_1h_artifactgarona_d_01]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue] Kingsbane [/color][/h3]
[spell=385627] is a single-target debuff with a 1-minute cooldown. Aim to be casting it on cooldown and aligning it with [spell=360194], as it will ramp faster during the window. Kingsbane is a two-part attack:
[ol]
	[li]An Instant hit of damage, generating a combo point[/li]
	[li]A 14-second damage-over-time effect which increases with every poison application during the effect[/li]
[/ol]
Deathmark is a strong boost to Kingsbane, as the duplicated poison applications greatly speed up the ramp time on Kingsbane's DoT effect.  
[/tab]

[tab name="Vanish" icon=ability_vanish]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=rogue] Vanish [/color][/h3]
[spell=1856] is a two-minute cooldown that enables the usage of [spell=381632]. This is the only remaining interaction with Stealth in Midnight for Assassination Rogues, and as such, Vanish is essentially just an enabler of Improved Garrote. In single-target, treat this as an extension of [spell=360194], whereas in mythic+, see it as a way to get a restealth.

Improved Garrote can be used in multiple situations, but two key ways to leverage it are in single-target and AoE rotations.
[ol]
	[li][spell=360194] increases the damage of [spell=703], so having Improved Garrote for this window is ideal to boost burst and single-target damage.[/li]
	[li][spell=1247227] spreads Improved Garrote to multiple targets without having to manually cast Garrotes on each target[/li]
[/ol]

General best practice for the cooldown is to cast it around the same time you would cast [spell=360194] to keep them synced. Make sure to also use the full 6 seconds of Improved Garrote to extend the duration of your empowered Garrote as long as possible. For Mythic+, use cases get a lot more complicated and depend heavily on your group, your route, and the situations you will find yourself in over the next 2 minutes.

Vanish in Mythic+ works best as pseudo-stealth, but you can also use it as an extension on your empowered garrotes in really long pulls. If you aren't sure when to use it or are uncomfortable planning ahead, cast it alongside your Deathmark to keep your main cooldowns synced.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c4][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c4][/icon] Assassination Rogue Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
The biggest optimizations for Assassination Rogue focus on energy efficiency, since this is the spec's main limiting resource.

[pad]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Pooling" icon=inv12_apextalent_rogue_implacable]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4] Pooling and Implacable [/color][/h3]
	Pooling is something often stated as a core feature of Assassination, and while it's true that pooling can have an impact (around 1.5% currently), the only way this materializes in the rotation is by playing around your Envenom timer. Casting [spell=32645] grants a buff for a short period of time, and talents such as [spell=455072] will ask you to then Envenom during this buff, starting a "chain". If you continue this chain for a long time, that's where the skill expression of Assassination is currently hiding.

In order to manage your energy and maximize your chain, you would want to press Envenom during the last 1-2 seconds of the current buff your character has. During cooldowns, [spell=1249809] means you would ignore this rule and burn all your energy for maximum efficiency. Assassination is an energy-locked spec, so making the most efficient use of energy is a core concept you will need to think about and master.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Assassination Rogue guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Assassination Rogue guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].



[tooltip name=NotesHighlight][color=q]Notes will appear here[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=darkest-fok][color=q]You can use Fan of Knives at 6 combo points to get the last combo point necessary for this, but these optimizations are only relevant in pure single-target. See the Shiv and Fan of Knives sections below for more details[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=shiv-cd][color=q]You can use Shiv on cooldown in single target on Deathstalker if you are talented into [spell=1267182]. This is a reasonably impactful min-max, but it adds another button into the mix, and you may want to hold onto Shiv for an enrage in mythic+ situations.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=vanish-gar][color=q]Depending on the time remaining in the fight, upcoming add waves, etc, it can be beneficial to instead hold Vanish. This is a very fight-dependent cooldown.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=pooling][color=q]It can be ~1.2% DPS gain to wait until the last 1-2 seconds of your current Envenom buff. This maximizes buff uptime while also managing your energy.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=ct-spam][color=q]In heavy aoe (10+ targets), this part can be ignored to spread bleeds even harder[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=precdct][color=q]Cooldowns can potentially be delayed in order to leverage [spell=381799 def=117673 rank=1] in higher keys. Always make sure your enemy survives the full length of your cooldowns, as this is always more important.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=scent][color=q]Usually you want to make sure that [spell=381799 def=117673 rank=1] is maxed in higher keys before going into cooldowns, so make sure you spread some bleeds beforehand.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=fok-st][color=q]With the Mythic+ build, you would instead want to press Fan of Knives in single target, and only use Mutilate upon reaching three stacks of [spell=1248774][/color][/tooltip]
